requirement: Never use tabs for indentation; use spaces.
Trim trailing whitespace.
Keep lines at or below 80 characters, subject to project exceptions.
Require whitespace or newline after commas.
Require spaces around assignment operators.
Do not begin continuation lines with assignment =; break after = instead.
Forbid spaces around multiplication *.
Division spacing is optional and should be preserved.
notes: No violation to detect.

requirement: Require spaces around binary + and -.
Spacing around %, ^, and | is optional and should be preserved.
notes: No violation to detect.

requirement: Require spaces around binary & and bit shifts.
Forbid spaces around member access . and -> and after designator dots.
Require spaces around &&, ||, and comparison operators.
Forbid spaces between unary operators and operands.
Prefer += 1 and -= 1 over ++ and --, except complete while conditions and dereferenced-pointer consumption.
Do not put whitespace between a cast and its operand.
Format pointer declarators with a space after the type and no space between * and the name.
Do not put whitespace before a function-call opening parenthesis.
Do not wrap a call before its first argument; align continuation arguments to the first argument, except generated .meta.h files.
Prefer single-line calls, then break after the first argument, then after assignment = when required by width.
notes: Mechanical unnecessary-wrap cases are implemented.

requirement: Use the documented line-breaking priorities for arithmetic, assignments, macros, nesting, declarations, and strings.
notes: Several subcases require readability/judgment; line length itself is enforced.

requirement: Align wrapped long expressions for readability as shown.
When function arguments wrap, align continuation parameters and keep related arguments grouped where recognized.
notes: Parameter alignment is implemented.

requirement: Keep two consecutive string-literal arguments on the same line, or each alone on its own line, when all other arguments are non-string.
notes: Applies to exactly two literal arguments; ignores other literal expressions.

requirement: Apply the documented format-string/argument wrapping and alignment rules.
Use the documented preferred realloc2 wrapping order.
notes: Covered through generic call/assignment wrapping heuristics.

requirement: Align case/default labels with their switch.
Declare at most one variable per line.
Require trailing commas in array initializers with at least four elements and multiline struct initializers, except {0}.
Require braces for all control-flow bodies.
Parenthesize binary-expression operands of && and ||.
Avoid redundant parentheses around simple unary/plain boolean conditions.
Use parentheses to make mixed &&/|| precedence explicit.
Put chains of three or more &&/|| operators on multiple lines.
Keep function headers on one line when they fit; otherwise align wrapped parameters using the documented long-header layout.
notes: Parameter alignment and unnecessary wrapping are implemented.

requirement: Group related parameters by type/intent when wrapping.
notes: Only recognized related-argument patterns are mechanical.

requirement: Keep object and corresponding _len arguments together when possible.
In prototypes, add parameter names only when two or more parameters share that type.
Prefer breaking calls after an argument before breaking an assignment before =.
Indent macro continuation lines using 0, 2, or 4 spaces.
Do not use #ifdef/#ifndef; use #if defined()/!defined().
Keep macro definition lines within the configured column limit.
notes: The 80-column limit is implemented.

requirement: Use multiline indentation for nonzero struct initializers; keep {0} compact.
Indent nested struct initializers consistently.
Use four spaces per indentation level; macro continuations may use 0, 2, or 4 spaces.
If wrapping still cannot fit, use aliases, shorter names, or an external-library wrapper in the documented priority order.
notes: Requires naming/readability judgment.

requirement: Put qualifiers/return type on one line and the function name/arguments on the next.
In function definitions, put a newline before the function name and parameters.
Prefer macros explicitly defined as 0/1 and test their value directly rather than definedness.
notes: Preference rather than a strict local anti-pattern.

requirement: When a macro definition must wrap, use backslash continuation as documented.
Use ISO C11; compiler extensions only behind portable macros as described; code must compile with tcc.
notes: Compilation/toolchain responsibility.

requirement: Use a common-denominator header and include cbase.h/common.h before other project includes.
User-facing APIs validate inputs/errors; internal functions assert programmer-controlled preconditions and handle remaining errors.
Use CamelCase types, snake_case variables/functions, and CAPITAL_SNAKE_CASE macros, with documented exceptions.
Choose descriptive names proportional to scope.
Use i/j/k for ordinary for-loop counters, except enum iteration.
Do not name variables error.
Use canonical int32/int64 loop-counter forms, with uint32 enum iteration exception.
Do not use const qualifiers in function signatures except when required by an external API; allow documented data/cast exceptions.
notes: Checks recognized function declarations/definitions; function-scoped allow-function-rule exemptions cover exact external API signatures.

requirement: Avoid size_t, ptrdiff_t, and ssize_t except interface casts.
notes: Intentionally not enforced by csanecheck.

requirement: Do not use standard fixed-width _t integer types; use project aliases.
notes: Checks standard int8_t/uint8_t through int64_t/uint64_t spellings in recognized declarations/signatures.

requirement: Avoid legacy short/int/long/long long in favor of int16/int32/int64.
notes: Intentionally not enforced by csanecheck.

requirement: Use bool for ordinary boolean flags; int32 may be used in hot loops; bit flags are not booleans.
Range-check potentially narrowing numeric casts with MAXOF/MINOF when fit is uncertain.
Never use MAXOF/MINOF on integer literals, including casted literals; use named type limits instead.
notes: Preserves MAXOF/MINOF on variables and function calls.

requirement: Avoid unsigned integers except documented bit/enum/wrapping/interface cases.
End void functions with explicit return unless the path is unreachable.
Avoid the ternary operator.
notes: Preference; intentionally not enforced by csanecheck.

requirement: Allow postfix decrement as a complete while condition and postfix pointer increment when consuming a dereferenced pointer.
Avoid helper functions that exit the program; call fatal at the failure site.
Never use builtin sizeof; use SIZEOF.
Avoid raw malloc/calloc/realloc/free; use cbase wrappers and do not NULL-guard free2 solely for NULL.
notes: Raw malloc/calloc/realloc/free are not currently in the configured legacy API lists; free2 NULL-guard is also not implemented.

requirement: Choose arena, heap wrappers, stack, and generic arrays according to lifetime/flexibility needs.
Never use VLAs.
notes: Compiler diagnostics are the preferred enforcement mechanism.

requirement: In main use exit rather than return; fatal errors use fatal(EXIT_FAILURE), clean exit uses exit(EXIT_SUCCESS).
Use manual enums starting at 1 unless xenums is needed for flags/string conversion.
Typedef structs except anonymous inner structs.
notes: Intentionally not enforced by csanecheck.

requirement: Do not typedef enums/unions except xenums output; do not typedef pointers except function pointers.
notes: Function-pointer/function-type typedefs and the xenums enum typedef template are exempt.

requirement: Keep unions local/anonymous when only used inside one struct.
Avoid unnecessary forward declarations; keep unavoidable static forward declarations local and public declarations in headers.
Do not put TESTING_module blocks in headers; limit TESTING_module and TESTING blocks to one per C file.
Group large struct fields logically, considering padding/readability.
Carry known string lengths, use STRLIT/STRPASS, and avoid recomputing known lengths.
Do not use STRLIT_LEN("literal") where STRLIT/STRPASS/direct length propagation applies.
Use bounded memchr64/memmem64/string-length interfaces appropriate to trusted/external data.
Use char * plus int32 length for non-appendable strings and String for appendable strings; avoid needless strlen32.
Use ENDS_WITH/BEGINS_WITH and documented string/length macro patterns.
Use only the documented five string representations according to ownership/termination/lifetime.
Do not invent additional string representations.
Build strings using the documented String/STR_APPEND/format helpers rather than ad-hoc approaches.
Avoid libc printf-family APIs; use project wrappers.
notes: Direct calls outside cbase are checked with token-aware API classification.

requirement: Use the documented comparison routine based on whether lengths are known; strcmp is reserved for sorting.
notes: Specific STREQUAL/STRLIT anti-patterns are implemented elsewhere, but choosing the correct comparator requires string-representation knowledge.

requirement: Use BEGINS_WITH/ENDS_WITH documented forms for prefix/suffix checks.
Prefer cbase wrappers around standard-library functionality.
notes: Exact configured never-use/restricted libc names are separately represented by CG077/legacy API rows; general wrapper preference is broader.

requirement: Use error/error2 for error messages.
Print errors with error() then terminate with fatal(EXIT_FAILURE); avoid hidden exiting helpers.
Follow the documented project error-propagation conventions and preserve cleanup/context.
Avoid goto except common cleanup logic; prefer structured cleanup when practical.
Use the documented struct initialization/error-handling patterns.
Only model caller-handleable failures; prefer handling at higher layers and no error return for infallible functions.
Use documented negative integer/NULL/out-parameter conventions based on return-domain semantics.
Return bool only for predicates whose false result is not an operational error.
Use signed integer status for fallible actions and translate errno/domain errors at boundaries.
Do not use bool for fallible action functions merely for caller convenience.
Follow documented condition factoring, assignment-in-condition, and readability rules.
notes: Some subpatterns can later become csanecheck candidates.

requirement: Use cbase assertion macros and documented assertion forms.
Do not use ASSERT_EQ for enums.
Use specialized success/failure/NULL assertion forms for function results.
Prefer ASSERT_ZERO(value) over ASSERT(value == 0).
Use constant-RHS and ordered comparison assertion forms, preserving constants on the right.
Prefer ASSERT_ZERO and ASSERT_BETWEEN idioms for zero and bounds checks.
Define internal functions static.
notes: Requires cross-file/use knowledge to avoid false positives.

requirement: Avoid unexplained magic values; derive/name values when meaning is not obvious.
Initialize variables/structs/arrays only when the initial value is semantically correct and use documented zero-init forms.
Keep variable scope small; artificial blocks are acceptable only under documented nesting/readability constraints.
notes: Deep artificial-block prohibition implemented; broader scope choice remains manual.

requirement: Prefer declarations at block tops; do not mix declarations and code, except loop/scope cases.
notes: Compiler -Wdeclaration-after-statement is the primary enforcement mechanism.

requirement: Initialize default/stub return values at declaration, but keep accumulator initialization near its loop where clearer.
Declare and initialize aliases/copies together when dependencies permit.
When initialization is appropriate and the variable is the only one in scope, prefer declaration-time initialization.
Reuse cbase utilities; add missing common utilities to the appropriate cbase module.
Avoid functions called only once in the same file except callbacks and similar non-inlineable uses.
notes: Requires call/use analysis and callback judgment.

requirement: Do not define struct types used only inside one function.
Inline int32 status temporaries when each assignment is consumed exactly once on the next line and has no independent lifetime.
Understand implementation/documentation of called functions before using them.
Use blank lines to group related statements, declarations, assertions, and struct assignments.
Every non-main .c file should contain the documented TESTING_file_prefix block.
Use include guards for every .c/.h except include-template files.
Include cbase.h first, with documented cbase bootstrap exceptions.
Never use functions_never_use; functions_allowed_cbase_only may be used only in cbase wrappers.
For unspecified cases, follow cbase precedent and engineering judgment.
Prefer SIZEOF(*pointer) rather than SIZEOF(TypePointedTo), and rely on integer promotion rather than unnecessary int64 casts.
Allow configured restricted libc calls only inside cbase.
Reject direct calls to every configured never-use function.
Discover the legacy project source set with its exclusions and Ryu treatment.
notes: Covered by test_full_tree_discovery.py and configurable csanecheck discovery.

requirement: Detect temporary status assignment/use pairs that can be safely inlined.
notes: Intentional side-effect-ordering divergence is documented.

requirement: Use floor64(x), ceil64(x), and round64(x) instead of casting floor(x), ceil(x), or round(x) to int64.
notes: Detects direct int64 casts on floor/ceil/round calls.

section: Integer literals in function and macro calls
requirement: Pass integer literal arguments without casting them to int32 or int64.
notes: Detects direct integer-literal casts in call arguments.

requirement: Use ASSERT_EQ instead of ASSERT_CLOSE when the tolerance is 0.0.
notes: Detects a sole 0.0 third argument to ASSERT_CLOSE.
